**8B.5 Research Note: Joko Widodo, 2024**

Bottom line: **mixed, leaning negative.** Jokowi showed real follow-through in a few technocratic systems, especially macro management, health, and crisis response. But coordination across politics, party structures, election-adjacent institutions, Papua, and late-term coalition management was uneven and often contaminated by patronage, coercion, and weak accountability.

**Accepted claims**
- **BI raised rates preemptively to defend rupiah stability and keep inflation in target** | Bank Indonesia | 2024-04-30 | https://www.bi.go.id/en/publikasi/laporan/Pages/Laporan-Kebijakan-Moneter-Triwulan-I-2024.aspx  
  - Claim: BI used preemptive monetary tightening and coordinated policy tools to preserve stability. This is strong evidence of disciplined macro coordination and follow-through.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **IMF says Indonesia’s fiscal and monetary frameworks remained prudent, credible, and shock-ready** | IMF | 2024-06-14 | https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2024/06/14/pr24221-imf-staff-completes-2024-article-iv-mission-to-indonesia  
  - Claim: IMF judged the macro framework coherent and resilient, which supports a reading of sustained coordination across core economic institutions.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **World Bank says Indonesia’s robust macro framework helped attract investment** | World Bank | 2024-06-24 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/06/24/indonesia-economy-projected-to-remain-resilient  
  - Claim: The World Bank credited Indonesia’s policy credibility and prudent macro management, indicating functioning cross-ministry coordination in economic governance.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **JKN redistribution mechanism used workload ratios, quality standards, and monitoring** | WHO Indonesia | 2024-10-29 | https://www.who.int/indonesia/id/news/detail/29-10-2024-less-burden--better-care--moh-and-who-accelerate-jkn-redistribution  
  - Claim: The health ministry and WHO used explicit operational criteria, monitoring, and patient choice to rebalance care. This is good evidence of real follow-through in a large public system.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Indonesia and WHO trained rapid-response teams in 514 districts** | WHO Indonesia | 2024-08-30 | https://www.who.int/indonesia/news-room/item/30-08-2024-indonesia-ramps-up-capacities-to-detect-and-respond-to-outbreaks-of-emerging-and-epidemic-prone-diseases  
  - Claim: The government built a nationwide operational network for early detection, verification, field investigation, and response. That shows concrete coordination and territorial reach.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Jokowi ordered an audit of government data centres after the ransomware attack** | Reuters via SCMP | 2024-06-28 | https://www.scmp.com/news/asia/southeast-asia/article/3268495/jokowi-orders-audit-indonesias-data-centres-after-cyberattack  
  - Claim: Jokowi reacted to a serious digital failure with an audit rather than denial or mass punishment. This is limited but real evidence of corrective follow-through.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2

- **Jokowi ordered rapid mitigation after the alleged taxpayer-data breach** | ANTARA News | 2024-09-19 | https://www.antaranews.com/berita/4345027/presiden-jokowi-minta-perlunya-mitigasi-soal-kebocoran-data-npwp  
  - Claim: He directed Kominfo, Finance, and BSSN to respond quickly, showing a coordinated crisis response across agencies.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.2

- **Jokowi formally transferred power to Prabowo on inauguration day** | Sekretariat Kabinet Republik Indonesia | 2024-10-20 | https://setkab.go.id/en/farewell-welcome-ceremony-for-indonesias-president-from-jokowi-to-prabowo-subianto/  
  - Claim: The constitutional handover happened on schedule, which is evidence that the succession mechanism still functioned.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.1

- **Jokowi publicly advanced Nusantara as tangible progress** | Presidential Secretariat of the Republic of Indonesia | 2024-08-14 | https://presidenri.go.id/siaran-pers/presiden-jokowi-resmikan-plaza-seremonial-sumbu-kebangsaan-di-ibu-kota-nusantara/  
  - Claim: He kept the flagship capital project moving with public milestones and ceremonial delivery, showing executive follow-through on a major program.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.2, 8B.1

- **Golkar picks Jokowi loyalist as leader** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-08-21 | https://theprint.in/world/indonesias-golkar-party-picks-influential-jokowis-top-loyalist-as-leader/2231679/  
  - Claim: Jokowi’s political network could still move the party apparatus enough to install a loyalist, preserving influence after office. This shows control over party structures, but in a patronage-heavy way.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4

- **Outgoing president gives cabinet jobs to Prabowo loyalists** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/outgoing-indonesian-president-widodo-names-prabowo-aides-to-cabinet-3576652  
  - Claim: The reshuffle smoothed transition politics by placing Prabowo-linked figures into office. That reflects network management, but not clean administrative discipline.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4

- **Bawaslu/Kominfo/police cyber task force targeted hoax content** | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/indonesia/freedom-net/2024  
  - Claim: The state built an election-period monitoring structure across agencies, showing real mobilization capacity. But the same report says the system was overbroad and coercive, so this is only partial positive evidence.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 4B.6

- **Indonesia’s security forces used tear gas and water cannon during the election-law crisis** | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-08-22 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/protests-across-indonesia-as-parliament-delays-change-to-election-law-3582501  
  - Claim: The state could move forces quickly against unrest, but the response was coercive and suggests control often substituted for clean discipline.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 4B.2

- **Papua abuses continued and accountability remained weak** | U.S. Department of State | published 2025-08-12; covers 2024 | https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128570.html  
  - Claim: The report says abuses persisted in Papua and officials were not systematically investigated or punished. That is strong negative evidence on control, discipline, and enforcement inside security institutions.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 4B.2

- **HRW says security forces committed grave abuses in Papua and were seldom held to account** | Human Rights Watch | 2024-09-18 | https://www.hrw.org/report/2024/09/18/if-it-s-not-racism-what-is-it/discrimination-and-other-abuses-against-papuans-in  
  - Claim: Security-force discipline was weak in a contested region, with serious abuses and limited punishment. This is the clearest negative evidence on state control through the security apparatus.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 4B.2, 4B.6

- **World Bank debars Jokowi-era project over overbilling and improper family hiring** | World Bank | 2024-07-10 | https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/10/world-bank-group-debars-pt-lppslh-konsultan  
  - Claim: A Jokowi-era project had procurement favoritism and weak discipline in implementation. This is negative evidence for clean follow-through across implementing agencies.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.4, 8B.2, 7B.9

- **Reuters end-of-term analysis: patronage, dynastic politics, weaker institutional integrity** | Reuters via ThePrint | 2024-10-14 | https://theprint.in/world/analysis-a-decade-of-jokowi-indonesias-democracy-icon-leaves-illiberal-legacy-critics-say/2310394/  
  - Claim: Reuters’ broad assessment is that Jokowi’s decade ended with patronage and weakened institutions. That is the strongest general negative signal against consistent internal discipline.  
  - IDs: 8B.5, 8B.3, 8B.4, 7B.9

**Search gap**
- I did not find a single whole-of-government internal audit, cabinet performance review, or formal coordination scorecard that directly measures discipline across the entire state. This judgment is therefore inferential, built from the strongest visible indicators: macro and health systems worked relatively well, while Papua, election politics, and patronage-linked staffing show major coordination failures and selective discipline.
